findings.title: Moon (Observed Sensor Beacon + Ephemeris Lock)
findings.subtitle: Measured at (933.5, 121.5) px · pose fit residual 0.00 px

evidence.verificationMethod: Measured in the image's pixels
limitations: Single celestial beacon (Moon) + horizon lock; no stars were held out for verification.
Without a verified WCS the detection has no sky position; the predicted Moon carries the ephemeris position.
The light centroid of a partly lit or saturated Moon is offset from the disk center; that bias is not modeled.

findings.title: Moon (Predicted Ephemeris)
findings.subtitle: Predicted Moon · 0.002 AU · Alt +32.2° · Inside Camera FOV

evidence.verificationMethod: Predicted for the given time and place; not measured in the image
limitations: Predicted from the given time and place with ERFA's analytic theories; not measured in any image.
Seen from the given place at sea level (topocentric): its parallax is applied, and its right ascension and declination are astrometric (light time only).
Its altitude and azimuth are apparent and airless: refraction at 1010 hPa and 10 degrees C (Saemundsson 1986) would lift it to +32.19 degrees, and the real air differs most near the horizon.

Its uncertainty, 44.1 arcsec, adds the method's documented worst error (18.5 arcsec here), 0.00 for light deflection applied as for a star, 13.8 for UT1 - UTC taken as 0 (within 0.9 s), 5.2 for a place up to 9 km above sea level, 1 for polar motion, and 5.6 for the time scale.

The moment is UTC, later than the leap seconds announced so far (to mid 2027), so TT may be off by up to 9 s of leap seconds not yet known (ERFA calls the year dubious); UT1 is taken as UTC, within 0.9 s, if the IERS keeps it so.
